name: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417) / Work and Holiday visa (subclass 462)

requirement_groups.name: Working Holiday visa (417) — reciprocal arrangement countries

value.note: up to 35 for a small number of eligible countries including Canada, France, Ireland

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being between 18 and 30 (up to 35 for a small number of eligible countries) at the time of application.
This requires sufficient funds to support yourself for the initial part of the stay.

requirement_groups.name: Work and Holiday visa (462) — other partner countries

value.note: up to 35 for a small number of eligible countries including Argentina, Chile

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being between 18 and 30 (up to 35 for a small number of eligible countries) at the time of application.
This requires sufficient funds to support yourself for the initial part of the stay, and typically a letter of support from your home government for eligible nationalities requiring one.

evidence_required.document: 3 months' specified work in a regional area (for second/third-year extension eligibility)

outcome.duration_length: 12 months, extendable to a 2nd and 3rd year with specified regional work completed each year

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL OUTLIER worth flagging prominently: unlike every other country's working holiday route in this dataset (UK Youth Mobility, Netherlands Working Holiday), Australia's version can be extended to a SECOND and even THIRD year — but only by completing specified work (commonly agricultural/regional work) for at least 3 months in a designated regional area each qualifying year. This makes it structurally closer to a genuine multi-year working-visa pathway than the strictly single-year, non-extendable versions seen elsewhere in this dataset, while still remaining fully terminal (leads_to_pr: false, no switchable_to targets) — it never converts into a settlement route regardless of how many years are completed. Two parallel visa subclasses (417 for one set of reciprocal-arrangement countries, 462 for a separate set of partner countries) exist for essentially the same purpose — modeled as two groups under one route rather than two separate files, since the functional product (a working holiday) is identical even though the specific eligible-country lists and administrative subclass numbers differ.
